question: Which of the following is needed for the formation of haemoglobin?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Fe**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Iron is needed for the formation of haemoglobin.
 
• Haemoglobin is a part of red blood cells that carry oxygen and remove carbon dioxide (a waste product) from the body.
 
• Iron is mostly stored in the body in the haemoglobin.
 
• About one-third of iron is also stored as ferritin and hemosiderin in the bone marrow, spleen, and liver.
 
• Red blood cells can't transport enough oxygen to body tissues if they don't have enough iron. 
 
• Iron deficiency causes anaemia.
 
• Sources of iron are meat, fish, liver, eggs, green vegetables, turnip, germinating wheat grains and yeast.
